That includes how the dots interact with light and electricity. It also includes their magnetic properties and at what temperature they melt. One useful quality that changes with a quantum dot’s size is its color. Usually, “if you want to make different colors with molecules, you would choose a new molecule,” Linke said. That is, a new set of atoms arranged in a different structure. But changing a quantum dot’s size can change its color without changing its molecules. A provocative role for technologists in product innovation Product design is in a moment of profound change and redefinition as technologies like artificial intelligence (AI) and spatial computing dramatically affect computing experiences. AI, especially, may have only minor impacts on interface design but will significantly impact the holistic product or ecosystem experience. Spatial computing, on the other hand, will change human-computer interactions and unmoor our understanding of what a computer is. In this innovation cycle, product design requires a wider perspective of platforms and interconnections between technologies, creating a strong need for technologists and designers to be in the process together. For successful products and businesses, innovation is perpetual. There is a never-ending search to find the next new thing that enhances the user experience, extends product reach, expands revenue, or all three simultaneously. Product design makes innovation less daunting and increases chances for success because it is a multidisciplinary process with structures and frameworks to catalyze innovation. Technologists have a role in the process that expands beyond simply validating the technology or concept, which is their customary responsibility. Before discussing the nontraditional ways technologists participate in product innovation, let’s conceptually examine innovation and product design. The word innovation has a simple meaning — to introduce something new or a novel method of doing something — yet we frequently inflate it to mean something magical, grandiose, and world-changing. She manages to strike the perfect blend of accessible and comprehensive so that everyone from founders to practitioners understand the critical role product marketing plays in successful companies and what good looks like at every stage of growth. Though I think what I appreciate the most about this book is that when it comes to marketing and driving product adoption, even though she introduces four fundamentals of product marketing, the first and most critical to get right is customer insight. **Summary of the passages**

1. **Historical context (2005)**
   - In 2005 Microsoft’s Internet Explorer was set as the default search engine on Windows.
   - Google’s legal chief, **David Drummond**, sent Microsoft an angry letter accusing the default setting as anticompetitive.
   - Drummond’s letter argued that problems with default settings are worsened by how changes to defaults are handled and that most end users **“do not change defaults.”**

2. **Current antitrust discussion**
   - **Bellshaw** referenced Drummond’s letter to highlight what he sees as Google’s hypocrisy today.
   - Other search‑engine companies (DuckDuckGo, Brave, Microsoft’s Bing) use similar arguments to accuse Google of anticompetitive behavior through deals with Apple and others.
   - The **U.S. Department of Justice (DOJ)** has reiterated that Google has become the monopoly it once denounced.

3. **Potential legal outcomes**
   - The case is expected to continue for several weeks, becoming one of the biggest tech antitrust fights since the U.S. sued Microsoft in the 1990s.
   - If the judge rules against Google, the outcome could resemble the Microsoft settlement:
     - Microsoft was required to change its behavior and **share its APIs with third‑party developers**.
     - Microsoft was also banned from making anticompetitive and exclusive deals with computer manufacturers.
   - Google might be forced to **turn over all or most of the data it has collected** to other search engines so they can improve their products and attract more users.

4. **Data advantage claim**
   - The DOJ has stated that Google receives **16 times more data than Bing does every day.**

5. **Broader implications for Big Tech**

   - On **November 4, 2023**, Chelsea Women announced that coach **Emma Hayes** would leave at the end of the season to “pursue a new opportunity outside of the Women’s Super League and club football.”
   - Hayes had been in charge of Chelsea for almost two decades and had won **six WSL titles**.
   - The announcement was made by the club at **11 a.m. ET** in the U.S. and at **3 p.m. UK time**; Hayes had not seen or written the statement.

2. **Appointment as U.S. Women’s National Team (USWNT) Head Coach**
   - The **U.S. Soccer Federation** confirmed Hayes as the **10th full‑time head coach** of the USWNT on **Tuesday, November 14, 2023**.
   - Hayes will not begin coaching the USWNT until her final season with Chelsea ends in **May 2024** (potentially as late as **May 25** if Chelsea reaches the Champions League final).
   - She will be unavailable for U.S. international windows that begin **May 27** and **June 4**, and she will miss the **2024 CONCACAF Gold Cup** (February–March) and the **2024 Olympic Games** (July 25–August 9).

3. **Contract and Compensation**
   - Hayes will become the **highest‑paid women’s football coach in the world**, with a salary close to **$2 million per year**.
   - The U.S. Soccer Federation’s board approved the appointment on the same day as Chelsea’s press release, even though the contract details were not yet finalized.
   - Chelsea reportedly offered to **quadruple Hayes’ salary** to retain her, but the final deal was not disclosed.

4. **Transition Arrangements**
   - Hayes will remain **exclusively with Chelsea** through the end of the WSL and Champions League campaigns, and she will not work with the USWNT during international windows.
   - **Twila Kilgore** will serve as interim head coach until Hayes’ arrival in **May 2024** and will become a permanent assistant coach under Hayes thereafter.
   - The U.S. Soccer Federation has a hand‑off plan in place, with Kilgore and the technical staff working to transition responsibilities.

5. **Personal and Professional Motivations**
   - Hayes cited her **son, Harry (five years old)**, as a key reason for leaving Chelsea, expressing a desire to spend more time with him and to attend his school and sports events.
   - She also mentioned the recent death of her father and the need for a professional and personal change after **12 years** at Chelsea.

6. **Impact on Chelsea Women**
   - **Millie Bright**, Chelsea captain, expressed devastation at Hayes’ departure, noting Hayes’ role as a mentor, coach, friend, and life coach.
   - **Denise Reddy**, Hayes’ American assistant (former U.S. U‑20 coach), is likely to follow Hayes to the U.S.
   - **Paul Green**, Chelsea’s general manager, will remain at the club; it is unclear whether other technical staff will leave.
   - Chelsea has received applications for Hayes’ replacement but has not begun an official recruitment process. Hayes will meet weekly with Chelsea’s technical directors to develop a succession plan and may retain an ambassadorial role if it does not conflict with her USWNT duties.

   - Hayes will relocate to the U.S. after completing her Chelsea season, with a move to **Chicago** planned for next year and a subsequent relocation to **Atlanta** once U.S. Soccer’s combined headquarters and national training facility in Georgia is operational (exact date not set).

The text explains how to choose a class in *Baldur’s Gate 3* (BG 3).  
- **Class balance**: All 12 classes in BG 3, as in pen‑and‑paper D&D, are roughly balanced; there is no single “best” class. The choice depends on how the player wants to play.  
- **Combat vs. non‑combat**: While a class mainly defines combat style, its primary Ability Score also influences non‑combat skills.

  - *Clerics* and *Druids* are Wisdom‑based, making them perceptive and insightful.  
- **Character creation options**:  
  - **Origin characters**: Players can start as one of the NPCs already in the party. This is quick but locks the player into that character’s predetermined story.  
  - **Custom characters**: Players can choose race, background, and other details, giving more freedom to experience the full story.  
- **Class distinctions**: Traditional labels such as “caster vs. puncher” or “melee vs. ranged” are less useful in BG 3 because classes overlap, especially as they level up.
